name: Telmisartan + Amlodipine
meta: Prescription-only fixed-dose combination. Components – Telmisartan: Schedule H –
prescription only; Amlodipine Besylate: Schedule H – prescription only
sections: White to slightly yellowish crystalline powder, practically insoluble in water.
408.88 g/mol (base); 567.05 g/mol (besylate; 6.94 mg besylate ≈ 5 mg base)
White crystalline powder (besylate), slightly soluble in water.

Telmisartan: The ONTARGET trial (2008; 25,620 high-risk patients) showed telmisartan non-inferior to ramipril for CV outcomes, leading to approval for cardiovascular risk reduction. First approval/introduction: Patented 1991; approved 1999 (Boehringer Ingelheim). Amlodipine Besylate: On the WHO List of Essential Medicines and one of the most prescribed drugs worldwide; ALLHAT and ASCOT-BPLA established its outcome benefits. First approval/introduction: Patented 1982; approved 1990 (Pfizer).
Amlodipine causes arterial vasodilation; telmisartan blocks the RAAS activation it triggers and reduces amlodipine-related ankle oedema. Additive BP reduction with 24-h coverage.

Telmisartan Selectively blocks angiotensin II type 1 (AT1) receptors, preventing vasoconstriction and aldosterone release; partial PPAR-gamma agonism. Longest half-life among ARBs. Receptor / target profile: Selective AT1 receptor blocker with insurmountable binding; partial PPAR-gamma agonist.

Amlodipine Besylate Inhibits transmembrane influx of calcium through L-type channels in vascular smooth muscle and myocardium, causing peripheral arterial vasodilation and reduced blood pressure; dilates coronary arteries and reduces myocardial oxygen demand in angina. Receptor / target profile: Long-acting dihydropyridine L-type calcium channel blocker selective for vascular smooth muscle.
Minimal hepatic glucuronidation (inactive acylglucuronide); no CYP involvement
Summary: Bioavailability 42–58%; Tmax 0.5–1 h. >99.5% protein bound. Glucuronidated; biliary excretion. Half-life ~24 h.
Extensive hepatic (CYP3A4) to inactive pyridine metabolites
Summary: Bioavailability 64–90%; Tmax 6–12 h. ~97.5% protein bound. Hepatic metabolism (CYP3A4). Half-life 30–50 h (once-daily).
Essential hypertension in patients not adequately controlled on either agent alone
Replacement therapy in patients on both components separately
One tablet once daily, with or without food
May increase to telmisartan 80 mg + amlodipine 5–10 mg after 2 weeks if needed
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
No adjustment (not dialysable); monitor K and creatinine.
Mild–moderate: max 40 mg/day; biliary obstruction/severe: contraindicated.
Contraindicated in second/third trimesters; avoid in first.
Use only if no safer alternative.
Biliary obstructive disorders, severe hepatic impairment
Concomitant aliskiren in diabetes or eGFR <60
Obstruction of left ventricular outflow (e.g. severe aortic stenosis)
Haemodynamically unstable heart failure after acute MI
Fetal toxicity – stop as soon as pregnancy is detected
Hyperkalaemia – monitor potassium, especially with K-sparing diuretics
Renal artery stenosis, renal impairment – monitor creatinine
Acute kidney injury (bilateral renal artery stenosis)
ACE inhibitors, aliskiren (dual RAAS blockade – avoid)
CYP3A4 inhibitors (clarithromycin, ketoconazole, diltiazem) raise levels
Telmisartan: With or without food; avoid potassium-based salt substitutes.
Amlodipine Besylate: With or without food; grapefruit may increase levels.
Telmisartan: Serum potassium and creatinine at baseline and 1–2 weeks after start/dose change; BP.
Amlodipine Besylate: BP; ankle oedema; heart rate.

Telmisartan: Hypotension, tachycardia or bradycardia. Supportive care; not dialysable. Amlodipine Besylate: Marked peripheral vasodilation, hypotension, reflex tachycardia, shock. Supportive care; IV calcium gluconate; vasopressors.
Littlejohn et al., 2009 – factorial trial: combination produced greater BP reduction than monotherapy.
ONTARGET (NEJM 2008) – telmisartan non-inferior to ramipril for CV outcomes.
Stop and inform doctor if pregnant
Ankle swelling is common – report if severe
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
